regime_context: The detector shows a broad, two-tier precious-metals-led tape on the TSX: Gold Miners are the leader (score 1.8, breadth 0.93), Silver & Royalties the close challenger (1.63), then a gap down to Base Metals/Copper (1.31) and Oil & Gas (1.20). Nine of sixteen themes are trend-eligible, so this is not a one-narrative market; the absolute-trend gate does help on this market's history, so trend discipline is the honest leg to lean on, while momentum rank is only a focus lens.
emerging_watch: Watching Big Banks (rank 5, score 0.75, eligible, durability_bar 0.66, hurst_tag trend) — the only clear 'trend' hurst tag among the top five and a robustness that survives the metals complex. The condition that would retire this watch: ZEB.TO closes more than 3% below its 20-day high before the check-by date (fading trend), or conversely a confirmed rise in breadth above 0.6 alongside a durability_bar still above 0.6 would upgrade it from watch to a real contender for leadership if the metals complex cracks.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: XGD.TO (proxy) is eligible, leads with the highest durability_bar (0.66) and near-universal breadth (0.93), and is not crowded (z 0.54). Since the ONLY validated edge here is drawdown/shake-out avoidance via the absolute-trend gate — not return forecasting — the defensible lean is a vol-aware stay with the leader rather than a return call; the broad breadth means the leadership is cohesive, not a single-stock spike. Track record direction accuracy is 0.372 on n=86, so conviction must stay low despite high hit rate (which mostly reflects avoiding the wrong side).
evidence: gate_helps=true on this market (trend discipline cuts drawdown)
theses.dissent: Silver & Royalties is only 0.17 behind with nearly identical breadth and the same proxy (XGD.TO), so the leadership is not cleanly differentiated; gold's r10 of -0.0054 shows no recent thrust, and the macro backdrop is dominated by ai_tech headlines, not gold — the leader could be a stale carry-over rather than an active narrative.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes more than 5% below its 20-day high before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: The challenger at rank 2 (score 1.63) is nearly tied with the leader (margin 0.17), with similar durability_bar (0.63) and breadth (0.92), and also not crowded. Because the rotation gap is narrow, this is a coherent precious-metals complex rather than a single leader; the trend gate supports staying with an eligible, high-breadth theme. But it shares the XGD.TO proxy with gold, so the two calls are effectively one complex view, and direction accuracy on this desk's history is poor.
evidence: rotation margin vs leader only 0.173 (complex cohesion)
theses.dissent: It shares a proxy with Gold Miners, so it offers no diversification and may simply be the same trade counted twice; silver's volatility can be higher than gold and the hurst_tag is only mixed, so the trend is not clearly persistent.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms the TSX benchmark by 3% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Rank 3 (score 1.31) and eligible, with positive but weaker durability_bar (0.51) and breadth (0.67). The trend gate still applies, so staying long the eligible theme is defensible on a vol-aware basis, but the hurst_tag of mean-revert and higher crowding_z (0.91, still not crowded) warn that this is the weaker leg of the materials complex and more prone to give back.
theses.dissent: Hurst mean-revert plus a 0.91 crowding_z make this the most fragile of the top three; copper is macro-sensitive and the macro narrative is AI/geopolitics, not industrial demand, so a rotation away from materials would hit this first.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO closes more than 5% below its 20-day high before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
